flowRoot.flowPara: • Pacts allow you to specialize combat abilities to suit the current situation. Savagery Pact bolsters your offense, Vampiric Pact provides defense and healing, and Predation Pact allows you to keep up with escaping foes or flee dangerous areas quickly.
• Cripple reduces a foe's movement speed for one movement. Weaken reduces the damage of a foe's next attack.
• Switching Pacts often can be beneficial due to their on-activation bonus.
• Rending Claws is best used as the last attack in a turn. Weave (S) cards to your attack skills to increase the health loss effect even further.
• If you've drawn the attention of a boss monster, you can expect a big hit. Use Acute Coagulant to mitigate some of the damage.
• Verve Magnet is very versatile. You can create or close distance between yourself and an enemy or yourself and an ally, and it heals allies as well.
• Don't understimate Adrenaline Surge. The Kindleborne and the Traceless, in particular, can do a lot with an extra action.

• Causing a foe to "lose health" is different from dealing damage. Health loss can't be blocked by shields or reduced by armor and interacts different with certain skills (such as Rending Claws and Violent Transfusion).
• "Pact-bound foe" refers to the foe whom you struck to activate the Pact. A foe remains Pact-bound until you activate a new Pact to a new foe.
• You may activate a new Pact on the foe you are currently Pact-bound to. The new Pact replaces the old one.
• Bloodlust only copies strikes; not any secondary effects of the skill that generated the strike.
• Culling Claws' bonus effect is based on the foes total health lost. A foe with 325/400 health wouldn't lose any additional health; a foe with 300/400 would lose 2 health.
